title: Unique normalized comparison for one coefficient arrow
statement: Under the parent hypotheses fix one actual stage arrow a:s to t, one compactification c, and normalized adjunction data at s and t. There is a unique Change a.ringMap c between those data. It records scalar preservation and etale boundedness, the canonical witness-normalized compact-support projection isomorphism, its invertible counit-transpose exceptional mate, and the unit equation. No simultaneous choice or coherence is asserted [def-pur-finite-coefficient-adjoint-data].

source.place: Parent lem-pur-finite-coefficient-adjoint-comparisons, numbered proof steps; general separated finite-type extension via ordinary-etale closed support as recorded there.

proof.text: On ordinary etale sites apply the direct-image lemma to $g$. For the open $j$, extension by zero is exact and the stalks of $j_!M$ are those of $M$ on $U$ and zero off $U$. Extending a constructibility stratification of $U$ by the closed complement shows that $j_!$ preserves bounded constructibility and the cohomological range; it takes a flat constructible model of $K$ in $[a,b]$ (the schemes are Noetherian by Step 1) to a flat constructible model of $j_!K$ in $[a,b]$, so $j_!$ preserves $D^b_{ctf}$ with the same Tor interval. The specified $q_j$ of the open-tensor lemma is invertible. Hence $F_A^{et}=Rg_*j_!$ preserves $D^b_{ctf}$ and its specified $q$ is invertible. Scalar extension preserves the same domain.

proof.text: The affine-chart factorization and gluing lemma supplies finite affine closed charts for $f$. The chart lemma makes each restriction of $f_A^\times L$ bounded constructible finite-Tor. Take extrema of the finitely many bounds; these properties are local, so $f_A^\times L$ has them globally. Restrict its ambient adjunction to these full subcategories.

proof.text: For each affine-space projection apply the ordinary-etale affine coefficient-mate lemma: its counit-normalized comparison is invertible and is the specified twist reassociation.

source.place: Agent-written ordinary-etale extraction of the locality/chart argument

proof.text: For a closed $i$, use its injective support sequence, the K-flat comparison and the counit-identification lemma. Step 2 supplies their open and closed projection isomorphisms; Step 3 supplies all bounds. Thus $b_i$ is invertible. On each affine chart, composition of $q$ and mate pasting identify $u^*b_f$ with the composite of $b_i$, $b_\pi$ and the tensor/pullback identity. Stalk conservativity proves $b_f$ invertible; Step 4 transports it to the stated pro-etale functors.

proof.text: Construct the normalized projection from the compact-support site and tensor comparison. Its specified value on each retained origin fixes it uniquely. Transpose the inverse projection followed by the scalar-extended counit to define the mate. The chart/support arguments give its invertibility. Transpose the proposed unit equation and use naturality and the adjunction triangle identity; both sides transpose to the identity. Injectivity proves the unit equation. Normalization fixes the projection and counit transposition fixes the mate, so proof irrelevance gives uniqueness.
